key_insight: MXFP4 training does not have to produce different bits on different hardware or parallelism layouts. CertiSum’s key observation is that native FP32 accumulation of MXFP4 products is often already exact.
problem_solved: Identical MXFP4 inputs can yield different results across runs, GPU vendors, and parallelism layouts, complicating debugging, training audits, and agreement between training and inference engines.
method: Exploit the observation that FP32 accumulation of MXFP4 products is often exact.
Build on this property to make MXFP4 training bitwise invariant across execution settings; the supplied abstract is truncated before the detailed mechanism.
impact: Bitwise reproducibility could make low-precision training easier to debug, audit, and move between platforms. It could also help eliminate numerical discrepancies between training and inference engines.
visual_elements: Before-and-after diagram: identical inputs produce divergent outputs without CertiSum and matching bit patterns with it.
Arithmetic pipeline: MXFP4 operands → products → FP32 accumulation, highlighting exact summation.
Comparison grid spanning GPU vendors and parallelism layouts, with identical output bit patterns as the target.
Icons linking reproducibility to debugging, auditing, and training–inference consistency.
paper_title: CertiSum: Bitwise-Identical MXFP4 Training Across Platforms and Parallelism Layouts
paper_authors: Steve Rhyner, Yubo Gao, Stefan de Lasa, Sankeerth Durvasula, Nandita Vijaykumar
